project.title: Chronic antibiotic stress decouples ammonia oxidation from nitrite oxidation and reshapes nitrifying functional hosts in activated sludge
project.description: Biological nitrification is vulnerable to antibiotic contamination, yet how chronic combined antibiotic stress differentially affects ammonia oxidation, nitrite oxidation and the linkage between nitrification disturbance and host-associated resistance remains unclear. Here, nitrifying sequencing batch reactors were operated to investigate the effects of combined ciprofloxacin, sulfadiazine and tetracycline exposure on nitrification performance, nitrogen-cycling genes, resistome dynamics and nitrifying functional hosts. The antibiotic-amended reactor shifted from complete nitrification to nitrite-accumulating incomplete nitrification. Although NH4+-N removal was partly maintained after acclimation, intensified antibiotic loading caused sustained NO2--N accumulation, reduced NO3--N production and strong inhibition of nitrite oxidation rate. Gene profiles further revealed asymmetric responses of the two nitrification steps: amoABC and hao showed partial recovery, whereas nxrB remained consistently suppressed by 15.4-30.3%, explaining the decoupling between ammonia oxidation and nitrite oxidation. Antibiotic exposure also restructured the sludge resistome, increasing total ARG abundance by 17.3% while reducing ARG subtype richness. The significant correlation between ARGs and MGEs (R2 = 0.79, p <0.05), together with ARG-MGE colocalization, indicated enhanced mobilization potential. MAG-resolved analysis showed that several nitrogen-cycling hosts carried ARGs. A representative Nitrosomonas europaea-like MAG harbored ammonia oxidation genes, ARGs, MGEs and stress-associated modules, with MGE-enriched variable regions suggesting genomic plasticity. These findings demonstrate that chronic combined antibiotic stress decouples ammonia oxidation from nitrite oxidation, sustaining partial ammonium removal at the cost of nitrite accumulation and increased antibiotic resistance dissemination potential.
